why_tests_were_wrong: The old cfg loaded base_dir=. and discovered a user transcript directory relative to ambient cwd. A clean checkout has no such originals, and another cwd could point it at a different project lake. These tests were not self-contained units.
A factory test assumed real keys and live availability without supplying either. It checked host/account state instead of deterministic dispatch.

Google test called real availability/translation but conditioned all assertions on availability. An offline provider meant a successful no-op; the independent fake-availability RED proves0 translation calls could pass.
red_evidence: old-four-delivered.stdout.txt and old-four-baseline.stdout.txt retain actual3FAIL/1SKIP; not ignored
fixes: scraper cfg reads unchanged template then points company/key/transcript data at owned tmp_path; real render_original produces3TXT for two MSFT periods and one SNOW period; sample bytes and sentinel checked after tests.
Path open/iterdir/glob fail if tests try original ambient/project transcript/company/key paths. Missing-file test now targets absent owned path.
Original nonempty file assertions replace environment-dependent skips; completed-entry charcount/source and two-period summary URLs/nonzerochars independently asserted.
common cfg base_dir is tmp_path. Factory tests use explicit synthetic JSON keys and mock only availability; four key vectors verify priority/checked candidates/no client construction.

Translator test class forbids socket/DNS calls and uses controlled translatepy backend. Actual Google wrapper constructor/available/translate assertions, exact two calls and output remain mandatory; no network-dependent conditional empty pass.
